scoring_note: 1 point per correct answer; unanswered at timer expiry scores 0. Suggested tie-breaker: total response time.

stages.description: Basic knowledge of Nigerian road signs, traffic rules, required documents and rights of way.

questions.question: In Nigeria, what shape are most warning signs (e.g. 'bend ahead', 'narrow bridge')?
questions.correct_answer: Triangular
questions.explanation: Triangular signs warn of hazards ahead. Circular signs give orders; rectangular signs give information.

questions.question: A circular road sign with a red border generally means:
questions.correct_answer: Prohibition — something is not allowed
questions.explanation: Red-bordered circles are prohibitive/regulatory signs, e.g. 'No entry', 'No overtaking'.

questions.question: What must you do at a red traffic light?
options: Stop only if pedestrians are crossing
Slow down and proceed if clear
Stop completely behind the stop line
questions.correct_answer: Stop completely behind the stop line
questions.explanation: Red means a complete stop behind the stop line until the light turns green.

questions.question: A flashing amber (yellow) traffic light means:
options: Speed up before it turns red
The light is broken — ignore it
Proceed with caution, giving way where required
questions.correct_answer: Proceed with caution, giving way where required
questions.explanation: Flashing amber allows you to proceed carefully while giving way to pedestrians and other traffic as required.

questions.question: Which agency is primarily responsible for road traffic safety and driver's licensing in Nigeria?
questions.correct_answer: FRSC (Federal Road Safety Corps)
questions.explanation: The FRSC administers road safety, driver's licences and highway regulations in Nigeria.

questions.question: What is the FRSC national toll-free emergency number?
questions.explanation: Dial 122 (toll-free) to reach the FRSC in a road emergency or crash.

questions.question: The minimum age to obtain a driver's licence in Nigeria is:
questions.correct_answer: 18 years
questions.explanation: You must be at least 18 years old to hold a Nigerian driver's licence.

questions.question: In Nigeria, vehicles are driven on which side of the road?
questions.correct_answer: The right side
questions.explanation: Nigeria uses right-hand traffic: keep right, and overtaking is normally done on the left.

questions.question: A zebra crossing is designed for:
options: Pedestrians to cross the road safely
questions.correct_answer: Pedestrians to cross the road safely
questions.explanation: Zebra crossings give pedestrians priority; drivers must slow down and stop for people on the crossing.

questions.question: A red octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means:
questions.correct_answer: STOP
questions.explanation: The octagon is reserved for STOP: come to a complete halt before proceeding.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a document you are required to have for your vehicle?
questions.correct_answer: International passport
questions.explanation: Required papers include your licence, insurance, roadworthiness and proof of ownership — not a passport.

questions.question: A standard Nigerian driver's licence is issued with a validity of:
questions.correct_answer: 3 or 5 years
questions.explanation: FRSC issues driver's licences with 3-year and 5-year validity options.

questions.question: A triangular sign with an exclamation mark (!) means:
questions.correct_answer: General danger/hazard ahead
questions.explanation: The exclamation triangle is a general warning: slow down and be prepared for a hazard.

questions.question: A green traffic light means:
options: Proceed only if the junction is clear and safe
Pedestrians have right of way over you in all directions
questions.correct_answer: Proceed only if the junction is clear and safe
questions.explanation: Green permits you to go, but only when your exit and the junction are clear and it is safe.

questions.question: A road sign showing two children walking usually warns of:
options: No minors allowed on this road
A school or children crossing ahead
questions.correct_answer: A school or children crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Slow down near school zones — children may cross suddenly.

questions.question: Rectangular road signs are generally used to:
questions.correct_answer: Provide information or direction
questions.explanation: Rectangles are informative signs: directions, distances, facilities and services.

questions.question: Every vehicle in Nigeria must display:
options: Number plates at the front and rear
questions.correct_answer: Number plates at the front and rear
questions.explanation: Valid number plates must be fixed and clearly visible at the front and rear of the vehicle.

questions.question: When the traffic light changes from green to amber (yellow), you should:
options: Prepare to stop safely before the line
questions.correct_answer: Prepare to stop safely before the line
questions.explanation: Amber means stop if you can do so safely — never accelerate to 'beat' the light.

questions.question: A continuous (unbroken) white line in the centre of the road means:
options: Overtaking is allowed at any time
Do not cross or overtake across the line
questions.correct_answer: Do not cross or overtake across the line
questions.explanation: A solid centre line prohibits crossing or overtaking because visibility or conditions are unsafe.

questions.question: A broken white centre line means:
options: You may overtake when it is safe to do so
questions.correct_answer: You may overtake when it is safe to do so
questions.explanation: Broken lines allow crossing/overtaking, but only when you can see it is completely safe.

questions.question: The general speed limit for cars in built-up areas (towns and cities) in Nigeria is:
questions.correct_answer: 50 km/h
questions.explanation: In built-up areas the limit for cars is 50 km/h due to pedestrians, junctions and heavy activity.

questions.question: Before starting to drive, the first things to adjust are your:
questions.correct_answer: Seat and mirrors
questions.explanation: A correct seating position and properly set mirrors are essential for control and visibility.

questions.question: Seat belts must be worn by:
questions.correct_answer: The driver and all passengers
questions.explanation: Nigerian law requires the driver and all passengers to use seat belts on every trip.

questions.question: The 'No Entry' sign is best described as:
options: A blue square with an arrow
A red circle with a white horizontal bar
questions.correct_answer: A red circle with a white horizontal bar
questions.explanation: The red disc with a white bar means the road is closed to traffic in that direction.

questions.question: Where there is no footpath, pedestrians should walk:
options: In the middle of the road
questions.correct_answer: Facing oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: Facing traffic lets pedestrians see approaching vehicles and step aside in time.

questions.question: Sounding your horn near a hospital or in a marked 'silence zone' is:
questions.correct_answer: Prohibited
questions.explanation: Horns are banned in silence zones such as hospital areas; the sign shows a crossed-out horn.

questions.question: Third-party motor insurance covers:
options: All damage to your own car
Injury or damage you cause to other people and their property
questions.correct_answer: Injury or damage you cause to other people and their property
questions.explanation: Third-party cover is the legal minimum: it protects others against loss you cause, not your own vehicle.

questions.question: A certificate of roadworthiness confirms that:
options: The owner has paid income tax
The vehicle is mechanically fit to be on the road
questions.correct_answer: The vehicle is mechanically fit to be on the road
questions.explanation: Roadworthiness certifies the vehicle's brakes, lights, tyres and body are in safe condition.

questions.question: When approaching a junction with no signs or traffic lights, you should:
options: Slow down, look both ways and be ready to give way
Speed through quickly before others arrive
Sound your horn and continue at speed
questions.correct_answer: Slow down, look both ways and be ready to give way
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled junctions demand reduced speed and readiness to stop for crossing traffic.

questions.question: A learner driver in Nigeria must:
options: Display 'L' plates and be accompanied by a licensed driver
questions.correct_answer: Display 'L' plates and be accompanied by a licensed driver
questions.explanation: Learners must show L plates and drive under the supervision of a fully licensed driver.

stages.stage_name: Intermediate — Safe Driving Practice & FRSC Regulations
stages.description: Practical safe-driving behaviour: following distance, overtaking, speed limits, lane discipline and vehicle regulations.

questions.question: The 'two-second rule' is used to:
options: Keep a safe following distance from the vehicle ahead
questions.correct_answer: Keep a safe following distance from the vehicle ahead
questions.explanation: Pick a fixed point; if you pass it less than two seconds after the car ahead, you are too close.

questions.question: On wet roads or in rain, your following distance should be:
options: The same as in dry weather
At least doubled — about four seconds
questions.correct_answer: At least doubled — about four seconds
questions.explanation: Wet roads can double stopping distances, so double your gap to at least four seconds.

questions.question: In Nigeria (right-hand traffic), you should normally overtake other vehicles on the:
questions.correct_answer: Left side
questions.explanation: With traffic keeping right, overtaking is done on the left, returning right when safely clear.

questions.question: It is most dangerous to overtake:
options: At bends, hilltops, junctions and pedestrian crossings
questions.correct_answer: At bends, hilltops, junctions and pedestrian crossings
questions.explanation: Never overtake where your view of oncoming traffic or crossing hazards is blocked.

questions.question: The maximum speed limit for private cars on Nigerian expressways is:
questions.correct_answer: 100 km/h
questions.explanation: Cars are limited to 100 km/h on expressways (80 km/h on other highways, 50 km/h in town).

questions.question: The legal blood alcohol concentration (BAC) limit for drivers in Nigeria is:
questions.explanation: FRSC enforces a 0.05 g/100ml BAC limit; the safest choice is not to drink at all before driving.

questions.question: Using a handheld mobile phone while driving is:
options: Allowed if the call is short
questions.correct_answer: A punishable traffic offence
questions.explanation: Phone use while driving is an FRSC offence — it multiplies your crash risk. Park safely to make calls.

questions.question: FRSC requires commercial vehicles in Nigeria to be fitted with:
questions.correct_answer: A speed limiting device
questions.explanation: Speed limiters are mandatory on commercial vehicles to curb overspeeding, the top cause of crashes.

questions.question: The minimum legal tyre tread depth is generally:
questions.correct_answer: 1.6 mm
questions.explanation: Below 1.6 mm of tread, grip in the wet collapses and the tyre is illegal — check tyres weekly.

questions.question: When another vehicle is overtaking you, you should:
options: Swerve towards it to warn the driver
Maintain or slightly reduce your speed and keep right
questions.correct_answer: Maintain or slightly reduce your speed and keep right
questions.explanation: Help the overtaker pass safely; speeding up prolongs the manoeuvre and creates danger.

questions.question: The correct routine before changing lanes is:
options: Mirror — Signal — check blind spot — then Manoeuvre
questions.correct_answer: Mirror — Signal — check blind spot — then Manoeuvre
questions.explanation: The MSM routine with a blind-spot (shoulder) check prevents side-swipe collisions.

questions.question: You should signal your intention to turn:
options: In good time — at least about 30 metres before the turn
At the exact moment of turning
Only when other cars are visible
questions.correct_answer: In good time — at least about 30 metres before the turn
questions.explanation: Early, clear signals give other road users time to react to your intentions.

questions.question: Leaving a broken-down vehicle on the road at night without lights or reflectors is:
options: A serious hazard and an offence
Acceptable if you will return soon
questions.correct_answer: A serious hazard and an offence
questions.explanation: Unlit stationary vehicles cause fatal night crashes — use hazard lights and place your warning triangle.

questions.question: 'Tailgating' means:
options: Following the vehicle ahead too closely
questions.correct_answer: Following the vehicle ahead too closely
questions.explanation: Tailgating removes your stopping margin; if the car ahead brakes hard, you will hit it.

questions.question: At a zebra crossing, the right of way belongs to:
questions.correct_answer: Pedestrians on the crossing
questions.explanation: Slow down on approach and stop for anyone on or stepping onto the crossing.

questions.question: In heavy rain during the day, you should:
options: Drive with no lights to save the battery
questions.correct_answer: Switch on dipped (low beam) headlights
questions.explanation: Dipped headlights make you visible in rain and spray; hazard lights while moving confuse other drivers.

questions.question: If dazzled by the high beams of an oncoming vehicle at night:
options: Slow down and look towards the right edge of the road
Close your eyes briefly until it passes
Flash your lights repeatedly and speed up
questions.correct_answer: Slow down and look towards the right edge of the road
questions.explanation: Using the road edge as a guide keeps you on course until your vision recovers.

questions.question: Overloading a vehicle beyond its rated capacity:
options: Reduces braking efficiency and stability, and is an offence
questions.correct_answer: Reduces braking efficiency and stability, and is an offence
questions.explanation: Excess load lengthens braking distance, strains tyres and destabilises the vehicle.

questions.question: Young children travelling in a car should:
options: Sit in front without a belt
Sit in the back seat, properly restrained
questions.correct_answer: Sit in the back seat, properly restrained
questions.explanation: The back seat with an appropriate restraint is the safest position for children.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you should give way to:
options: Traffic already circulating in the roundabout
questions.correct_answer: Traffic already circulating in the roundabout
questions.explanation: Vehicles already in the roundabout have priority; enter only when there is a safe gap.

questions.question: Hazard warning lights should be used:
options: When your vehicle is stationary and causing an obstruction, or in an emergency
While driving normally in light rain
questions.correct_answer: When your vehicle is stationary and causing an obstruction, or in an emergency
questions.explanation: Hazard lights warn of danger or breakdown — using them while moving normally misleads other drivers.

questions.question: 'Defensive driving' means:
options: Fitting protective bars to your vehicle
Driving very slowly at all times
Anticipating hazards and the mistakes of other road users
Driving aggressively to defend your lane
questions.correct_answer: Anticipating hazards and the mistakes of other road users
questions.explanation: A defensive driver expects errors from others and always leaves room and time to respond.

questions.question: If you begin to feel sleepy while driving, the safest action is to:
options: Stop in a safe place and rest
Drive faster to finish the trip quickly
questions.correct_answer: Stop in a safe place and rest
questions.explanation: No trick beats sleep. A short nap in a safe place can save your life — fatigue kills.

questions.question: On long journeys, FRSC advises drivers to take a rest break:
options: About every two hours, or whenever tired
questions.correct_answer: About every two hours, or whenever tired
questions.explanation: Regular breaks keep reaction time sharp; fatigue builds up silently on long trips.

questions.question: When passing motorcyclists (okada) and cyclists, you should:
options: Give them extra clearance and reduce speed
questions.correct_answer: Give them extra clearance and reduce speed
questions.explanation: Two-wheelers can wobble or swerve around potholes — leave generous side space.

questions.question: Compared with private cars, tankers and trailers are subject to:
questions.correct_answer: Lower speed limits
questions.explanation: Heavy vehicles need far longer to stop, so their limits (e.g. 45–60 km/h) are lower than cars'.

questions.question: The recommended way to hold the steering wheel is:
options: Steering with the knees on straight roads
One hand resting at the bottom
Both hands on the wheel, about the 9 and 3 o'clock position
questions.correct_answer: Both hands on the wheel, about the 9 and 3 o'clock position
questions.explanation: Two hands at 9 and 3 give maximum control for emergency steering.

questions.question: When joining an expressway from a slip road (acceleration lane), you should:
options: Stop at the end of the lane and wait
Merge immediately at very low speed
Build up speed to match traffic and merge when there is a safe gap
questions.correct_answer: Build up speed to match traffic and merge when there is a safe gap
questions.explanation: Matching traffic speed lets you merge smoothly without forcing others to brake.

questions.question: Wearing a seat belt in a crash roughly:
options: Halves your risk of death or serious injury
questions.correct_answer: Halves your risk of death or serious injury
questions.explanation: Belts cut the risk of death for front-seat occupants by about 45–50% — buckle up every trip.

questions.question: At a railway level crossing without barriers or lights, you should:
options: Stop, look both ways and listen before crossing
Drive across as quickly as possible
Follow the vehicle in front without checking
questions.correct_answer: Stop, look both ways and listen before crossing
questions.explanation: Trains cannot stop for you. Cross only after confirming the line is completely clear.

stages.description: Defensive driving judgement: emergencies, skids, night/weather driving, crash-scene response and risk anticipation.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while driving, you should first:
options: Accelerate to escape the traffic around you
Switch off the engine and remove the key
Jump out of the moving vehicle
Pump the brake pedal, shift to a lower gear and apply the handbrake gradually
questions.correct_answer: Pump the brake pedal, shift to a lower gear and apply the handbrake gradually
questions.explanation: Pumping may restore pressure; engine braking and gradual handbrake use scrub off speed under control.

questions.question: If a tyre bursts at speed, you should:
options: Grip the steering firmly, ease off the accelerator and slow down gradually
Swerve quickly to the shoulder at speed
Switch off the ignition at once
Brake as hard as possible immediately
questions.correct_answer: Grip the steering firmly, ease off the accelerator and slow down gradually
questions.explanation: Hard braking or sharp steering after a blowout causes loss of control — decelerate smoothly first.

questions.question: 'Aquaplaning' (hydroplaning) happens when:
options: Tyres lose contact with the road on a film of water
questions.correct_answer: Tyres lose contact with the road on a film of water
questions.explanation: At speed on standing water, tyres ride on the water film and steering and braking stop working.

questions.question: If your car begins to aquaplane, you should:
options: Ease off the accelerator, keep the steering straight and avoid braking suddenly
Turn the wheel sharply to regain grip
questions.correct_answer: Ease off the accelerator, keep the steering straight and avoid braking suddenly
questions.explanation: Lifting off gently lets the tyres slow and regain contact; sudden inputs cause a skid.

questions.question: If your vehicle catches fire while driving:
options: Keep driving to the nearest mechanic
Continue slowly with the windows open
Open the bonnet fully to inspect the flames
Stop safely, switch off the ignition, get everyone out and away, then tackle only a small fire with an extinguisher
questions.correct_answer: Stop safely, switch off the ignition, get everyone out and away, then tackle only a small fire with an extinguisher
questions.explanation: Life first: evacuate upwind and call for help. Never fully open a burning bonnet — it feeds the fire air.

questions.question: On a highway, the warning triangle (C-caution) should be placed approximately:
options: On the roof of the vehicle
questions.correct_answer: 45 metres behind the vehicle
questions.explanation: About 45 m gives approaching traffic time to see and react before reaching your vehicle.

questions.question: To correct a rear-wheel skid, you should:
options: Ease off the pedals and steer gently in the direction the rear is sliding
Brake hard and steer away from the skid
questions.correct_answer: Ease off the pedals and steer gently in the direction the rear is sliding
questions.explanation: Steering into the skid realigns the car; harsh braking or power makes the slide worse.

questions.question: The most important rule for night driving is:
options: Follow the tail lights ahead closely
Use full beam at all times
Never drive faster than you can stop within the distance your headlights show
questions.correct_answer: Never drive faster than you can stop within the distance your headlights show
questions.explanation: If a hazard appears at the edge of your beam, you must be able to stop before reaching it.

questions.question: When meeting an oncoming vehicle at night, you should:
options: Dip your headlights to low beam
Keep full beam on for better vision
questions.correct_answer: Dip your headlights to low beam
questions.explanation: Dipping prevents dazzling the other driver — a dazzled driver may drift into your lane.

questions.question: During harmattan haze or fog, you should:
options: Drive at normal speed to exit the fog quickly
Use full beam to see farther
Use dipped headlights or fog lights, reduce speed and increase following distance
questions.correct_answer: Use dipped headlights or fog lights, reduce speed and increase following distance
questions.explanation: Full beam reflects off haze and blinds you; slow down and extend your gap — visibility can drop suddenly.

questions.question: Arriving first at a crash scene, your first action should be to:
options: Drive past quickly to avoid delay
Park safely, switch on hazard lights, protect the scene and call 122
questions.correct_answer: Park safely, switch on hazard lights, protect the scene and call 122
questions.explanation: Securing the scene prevents a second crash; then summon FRSC/emergency services on 122.

questions.question: A crash victim with a suspected neck or spinal injury should be:
options: Carried on someone's back to a car
Left in position and not moved unless there is immediate danger such as fire
Sat upright immediately to help breathing
questions.correct_answer: Left in position and not moved unless there is immediate danger such as fire
questions.explanation: Movement can turn a spinal injury into permanent paralysis — wait for trained responders unless danger forces evacuation.

questions.question: Total stopping distance is made up of:
questions.correct_answer: Thinking (reaction) distance plus braking distance
questions.explanation: You travel a long way while reacting before the brakes even begin to work.

questions.question: If you double your speed, your braking distance becomes roughly:
questions.correct_answer: Four times as long
questions.explanation: Braking distance rises with the square of speed — small speed increases cost big stopping distance.

questions.question: If the engine overheats, you should:
options: Open the radiator cap immediately to release pressure
Pull over safely, switch off the engine and wait for it to cool before checking
Pour cold water on the hot engine block
Keep driving to burn off the heat
questions.correct_answer: Pull over safely, switch off the engine and wait for it to cool before checking
questions.explanation: A hot radiator cap can erupt with scalding steam; cold water on a hot block can crack it.

questions.question: Sleeping inside a parked car with the engine and air-conditioner running is dangerous mainly because of:
questions.correct_answer: Carbon monoxide poisoning
questions.explanation: Exhaust fumes can seep into the cabin; carbon monoxide is odourless and can kill sleeping occupants.

questions.question: A 'black spot' on a road refers to:
options: A location with a history of frequent crashes
An oil stain on the tarmac
questions.correct_answer: A location with a history of frequent crashes
questions.explanation: Approach marked black spots with extra caution and reduced speed.

questions.question: Strong crosswinds on bridges and exposed roads most affect:
options: High-sided vehicles, motorcycles — and any vehicle's steering, so grip the wheel firmly
questions.correct_answer: High-sided vehicles, motorcycles — and any vehicle's steering, so grip the wheel firmly
questions.explanation: Sudden gusts can push you off line, especially when passing trucks or gaps in buildings.

questions.question: A long articulated truck ahead signals and swings wide before a junction. You should:
options: Flash your lights to hurry it up
Sound your horn and squeeze past
Hold back — it needs extra room to complete its turn
Quickly overtake through the gap it has opened
questions.correct_answer: Hold back — it needs extra room to complete its turn
questions.explanation: Long vehicles swing out before turning; the 'gap' will close on anything beside them.

questions.question: A defensive driver always maintains a 'space cushion', meaning:
options: Space around the vehicle that allows an escape route if something goes wrong
questions.correct_answer: Space around the vehicle that allows an escape route if something goes wrong
questions.explanation: Managing the space ahead, behind and beside you is the core of defensive driving.

questions.question: In an emergency stop with ABS brakes, you should:
options: Release the brake when the pedal vibrates
Press the brake firmly, keep it pressed, and steer around the hazard if needed
questions.correct_answer: Press the brake firmly, keep it pressed, and steer around the hazard if needed
questions.explanation: The pulsing pedal is ABS working — maintain firm pressure; ABS lets you steer while braking.

questions.question: When descending a long, steep hill, you should:
options: Ride the brakes continuously all the way down
Shift to neutral to save fuel
Engage a lower gear and use engine braking
questions.correct_answer: Engage a lower gear and use engine braking
questions.explanation: Engine braking controls speed without overheating the brakes; neutral or engine-off removes control.

questions.question: 'Brake fade' is caused by:
options: Overheating of the brakes from continuous heavy use
questions.correct_answer: Overheating of the brakes from continuous heavy use
questions.explanation: Overheated pads and fluid lose stopping power — a major danger on long descents.

questions.question: The safest approach to a flooded section of road is to:
options: Follow trucks through at their speed
Cross with the clutch fully pressed
Avoid it if possible; if you must cross, go slowly in a low gear and test your brakes afterwards
Speed through so the engine does not stall
questions.correct_answer: Avoid it if possible; if you must cross, go slowly in a low gear and test your brakes afterwards
questions.explanation: Water hides depth, washouts and open drains; wet brakes need gentle testing after crossing.

questions.question: An unsecured or protruding load on a vehicle:
options: Is a serious hazard to other road users and an offence
Is acceptable if tied loosely with rope
questions.correct_answer: Is a serious hazard to other road users and an offence
questions.explanation: Falling loads cause multi-vehicle crashes; loads must be secured and within legal dimensions.

questions.question: At night or in heavy rain, the two-second following rule should be extended to at least:
questions.correct_answer: Four seconds
questions.explanation: Lower visibility and grip demand a much bigger safety gap.

questions.question: A pedestrian suddenly steps into your path. The safest reaction is usually to:
options: Brake firmly while keeping control and staying in your lane where possible
Sound the horn and maintain speed
questions.correct_answer: Brake firmly while keeping control and staying in your lane where possible
questions.explanation: Controlled firm braking sheds the most speed; swerving into traffic often trades one crash for a worse one.

questions.question: FRSC requires vehicles to carry which safety items?
options: A fire extinguisher and a warning triangle (C-caution)
questions.correct_answer: A fire extinguisher and a warning triangle (C-caution)
questions.explanation: The extinguisher and C-caution are mandatory equipment checked at FRSC inspections.

questions.question: Brief 'microsleeps' while driving are a sign of:
options: Dangerous fatigue — stop and rest immediately
questions.correct_answer: Dangerous fatigue — stop and rest immediately
questions.explanation: A 3-second microsleep at 100 km/h means over 80 metres travelled blind.

questions.question: After long, fast expressway driving, when you enter a town your speed often:
options: No longer matters in built-up areas
Feels slower than it really is — check your speedometer
Feels faster than it really is
questions.correct_answer: Feels slower than it really is — check your speedometer
questions.explanation: Speed adaptation tricks your senses; trust the speedometer and drop to the 50 km/h limit.
